title: Exponential parity sample complexity below the mean-field scaling
status: Main result
summary: For every fixed gamma < 1 and fixed depth, full parity in dimension d requires exp(Omega(d)) samples under uniform IID training and the width-first posterior. For each n <= exp(c d), confidence failure is at least 1/16 with sample probability at least 3/4. This is the full-parity exponential result, not the still-open fixed-depth natural sparse-parity scale exp(Omega(k log(ed/k))).

title: Parity under standard-scaling neural-network Gaussian processes: superpolynomial and nearly exponential sample lower bounds at fixed depth
status: Proved side result; conventional proof with independent AI-agent reviews; the coercivity input of the typical-sample theorem is a Lean-verified theorem
summary: Usual NNGP scaling (exponent tuple (0,1,...,1,1)) at fixed depth, width first. Globally margined tanh networks: for large d, n <= exp(sqrt(d) log(d)/20) iid examples of full parity leave confidence failure >= 1/16 with probability >= 1-e^{-d/10}. Sign-only learner: for every bounded continuous nonconstant activation, depth and gain, every training set with n <= d^{sqrt(d)/10-1/2}/6000 leaves failure >= 1/4; d^k scale for fixed k-sparse parity. Typical samples, tanh: n <= exp(10^{-3} d loglog d/log d) leaves failure >= 3/8 with probability >= 13/16 for d >= d_0 (explicit but astronomically large), via a random-restriction form of the ABFR bound. exp(Omega(d)) is open; the subcritical proof's polynomial per-sample conditioning cost is false here, and a sharper lower bound shows that no matching upper bound exists.
